content:
- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the 30-day horizon.
- Forecast shows upward trend but fails to capture sharp downward corrections or sudden drops in later days.
- Overshoots occur after spikes in historical prices (e.g., after 85+ peaks, model jumps too high then fails to correct).
- Mean reversion is not adequately modeled — model holds too much upward bias after peaks, ignoring volatility decay.
- Late-period (last 5–10 days) forecasts are often too high, suggesting model overreacts to recent highs and fails to adjust for downward momentum.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to true price drops — often forecasts remain high while prices fall sharply.
- Forecast assumes smooth continuation of recent trend, ignoring sudden reversals or structural breaks (e.g., after 80–85 range, prices drop below 75).
